title: Sara goes to school
intro: A morning in the life of Sara, a nine-year-old in Tehran. This story practises the present tense of everyday verbs – wakes up, eats, goes, learns – and the words for school and family. Iranian schools start early, around 7:30, and the school week runs from Saturday to Wednesday or Thursday.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.en: Sara wakes up at six o'clock.

sentences.fa: مادر سارا چای و نان و پنیر می‌آورد.
sentences.r: mādar-e Sārā chāy o nān o panir mi-āvarad.
sentences.en: Sara's mother brings tea, bread and cheese.
sentences.faV: مادَرِ سارا چای و نان و پَنیر می‌آوَرَد.

sentences.fa: او کیف و کتاب‌هایش را برمی‌دارد.
sentences.r: u kif o ketāb-hā-yash rā bar-mi-dārad.
sentences.en: She picks up her bag and her books.
sentences.faV: او کیف و کِتاب‌هایَش را بَرمی‌دارَد.

sentences.fa: سارا با پدرش به مدرسه می‌رود.
sentences.r: Sārā bā pedar-ash be madrese mi-ravad.
sentences.en: Sara goes to school with her father.
sentences.faV: سارا با پِدَرَش به مَدرِسه می‌رَوَد.

sentences.en: The school is near the house.

sentences.fa: دوست سارا، لیلا، هم آن‌جا است.
sentences.r: dust-e Sārā, Leylā, ham ān-jā ast.
sentences.en: Sara's friend Leila is there too.
sentences.faV: دوستِ سارا، لَیلا، هَم آن‌جا اَست.

sentences.en: They say hello to the teacher.

sentences.fa: امروز سارا فارسی و ریاضی دارد.
sentences.r: emruz Sārā fārsi o riyāzi dārad.
sentences.en: Today Sara has Persian and maths.
sentences.faV: اِمروز سارا فارسی و ریاضی دارَد.

sentences.fa: او ریاضی را خیلی دوست دارد.
sentences.r: u riyāzi rā kheyli dust dārad.
sentences.faV: او ریاضی را خَیلی دوست دارَد.

questions.q: What time does Sara wake up?
What does Sara eat for breakfast?
Who goes to school with Sara?
Which subject does Sara like very much?

after: Bread, cheese and sweet tea – نان و پنیر و چای – is the classic Iranian breakfast, often with walnuts or herbs. Notice the compound verbs made with شدن: بیدار می‌شود 'wakes up' (literally 'becomes awake'), تمام می‌شود 'finishes' ('becomes complete'). Half of Persian verbs are built this way. Also notice ساعت شش 'six o'clock': ساعت means hour, clock and o'clock all at once.
